assessment.governing_intent: Prove that the actual sandbox_run_profile and github_profile constructors, using local transports, refuse multi-role worker launch unless role authority, exact candidate custody and durable outcome correlation are bound. A correctly bound real WorkerProvider must reach correlated success, rejection and restart readback through existing evidence ownership. Invocation ownership must survive provider/client exit while owned background work is active. The work must not add a sidecar state owner and must not claim live or shared-profile activation.
implementation_unknowns: Which work order is K1, and whether its durable WorkerProvider outcome/readback seam is DONE. WO-220209 is listed as DONE but its description reads as the disposition/provenance node, not clearly as K1.
The exact shape of the K1 outcome/readback seam and K2 orchestration entry points that the sandbox and GitHub profile constructors must bind.

Whether the current WorkerOutcome can carry every required correlation observable (role, invocation, attempt, candidate, finding/receipt), or whether revised Design Verification must justify extending the typed result contract.
How supervised background work started by an invocation is currently tracked. This determines how 'provider/client exit is not terminal while owned work is active' is enforced and proven.
Where the pre-launch binding guard best sits in each profile constructor so that bypassing it is detectable by a negative control.
material_risks: Predecessor K2 (WO-220402) is READY, not DONE. Starting now risks building against unproven or changing K2 orchestration interfaces.

The founder amendment adds deterministic post-death recovery/replacement semantics. There is a risk this expands K3 into Invocation Runtime supervision redesign rather than a composition compatibility proof. Implementation should stay within existing authority, attempt and budget policy and escalate genuine interface gaps to the K1/K2 owner.
Pressure to extend WorkerOutcome or add a RoleOutcomeRecord sidecar if correlation observables are missing. This is prohibited without separate review.
Tests could satisfy acceptance through mocked lifecycles instead of the production composition path, which violates the fixed decisions.
A local proof result could be misread as live or shared-profile activation authority. This is an explicit non-claim.
The UNKNOWN ownership/effect state must block replacement launch. Weak negative controls here could mask duplicate-actor launches.
assessment.next_action: Hold WO-220403 in TASKS. Confirm K2 (WO-220402) reaches DONE with retained proof, and identify K1 and confirm it is DONE with its durable outcome/readback seam proven. Then request a fresh Agent Ready assessment of this exact revision.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is a missing external prerequisite, not unresolved intent. Owner decisions are explicitly fixed: ownership, no sidecar state, the production path through composition, custody, landing and non-claims. The scope is one cohesive decision center, so SPLIT and CLARIFY do not apply. The acceptance predicate itself begins 'With K1/K2 predecessor proof', and the task's readiness rule requires every predecessor BIU to be DONE. The supplied text reports WO-220402 (K2) as READY, not DONE, and does not establish K1's completion. Without those predecessor artifacts, neither implementation nor independent verification of composition compatibility can proceed meaningfully. These dependency statuses are as reported in the task text and have not been independently verified here.
assessment.summary: Intent, ownership and non-goals are well specified. The K3 extent is cohesive: composition binding guards plus a compatibility proof over existing WorkerProvider and evidence seams. Acceptance is observable through named test surfaces and discriminating negative controls. However, the acceptance predicate is conditioned on 'K1/K2 predecessor proof', and the task's own readiness rule requires every predecessor BIU to be DONE. The listed K2 predecessor, WO-220402, is reported as READY, not DONE. K1's completion status is not stated. The work cannot be meaningfully executed or verified until predecessor proof exists.
assessment.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable. Constructors refuse missing or miscorrelated authority, custody and outcome binding before launch. A bound real adapter reaches correlated success, rejection and restart readback. Disconnecting correlation or bypassing the guard makes the proof fail. Owned background work retains invocation ownership through the terminal boundary. Named test files and an initial pytest command are supplied, and the proof policy asks for one discriminating negative control per failure class. A single independent verdict is meaningful for this cohesive extent, but only once K1/K2 predecessor proof exists to compose against. Before then the verdict would rest on assumed or stubbed seams, which the task forbids.
